subject: Clarify measurement windows for P50/P95 commitments — hosted API
messages:
From: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acme.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: acme-platform-sre@acme.com
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Measurement window for P50/P95 — need clarification

Irene, thanks for the draft SLA. Before we sign we need to clarify exactly how you measure P50/P95 for the hosted API. Two items in particular:

- Do you calculate p50/p95 on a per-tenant basis or across aggregate traffic?
- What measurement window do you apply (rolling 1m/5m/1h, calendar day, or monthly aggregates)?

Our SRE team is concerned that a 1-minute bucket could be noisy for our bursty traffic patterns. We'd like to understand whether Redwood can guarantee p50/p95 over a 5-minute rolling window or alternatively offer a per-customer averaging approach for monthly credits.

Can you send the precise definitions and an example calculation (with sample request distributions)? Amanda

--
Amanda Lee
Head of Platform Reliability, Acme Platform
amanda.lee@acme.com
From: irene.choi@redwood.com
To: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acme.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 12:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Measurement window for P50/P95 — need clarification

Amanda — thanks, and great questions. High level answers up front, details below:

- Redwood measures p50/p95 at the route+model level by default (aggregate across requests to that route/model in the region), but we can provide per-tenant breakdowns for customers on Dedicated or with enterprise reporting enabled.
- Measurement window for commitments in the hosted plan is a rolling 5-minute window for short-term SLO evaluation, with monthly aggregation used for credits/license calculations. We do not use 1-minute buckets as an SLA enforcement mechanism.

Attached is a short worked example and our exact calculation steps. Key points:
1) Rolling 5-minute percentiles are computed from all successful request latencies (server-side generation time + network egress) within each 5-minute window.
2) Monthly SLO compliance is evaluated by counting the number of 5-minute windows that breach the threshold and normalizing over total windows in the month to determine eligibility for credits.
3) For your traffic profile we can provide a per-tenant monthly percentile if you prefer credits evaluated against your tenant-specific distribution.

Ben (cc'd) — can you confirm operational implications and whether we need a small exception for special routing that Amanda mentioned on the call?

Best,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Director, Account Development (Enterprise Sales)
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 12:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Measurement window for P50/P95 — need clarification

Irene / Amanda — quick operational note: the rolling-5m approach is what our telemetry pipeline supports today across hosted customers. It reduces noise vs 1m buckets and is cheap to compute. Two caveats for Acme's burst pattern: 

- If Acme sends very heavy burst traffic that saturates a single model shard, you'll see short-lived p95 spikes that count as breached 5-minute windows.
- We can implement a mitigator: for customers on an enterprise plan we can exclude the top and bottom 0.5% of requests per-window for SLA evaluation to avoid outlier-induced breaches (this is a policy change and requires legal approval).

Karthik, can you estimate effort to expose per-tenant monthly percentile and the 0.5% outlier exclusion flag in the console?

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acme.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: acme-platform-sre@acme.com
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Measurement window for P50/P95 — need clarification

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups from our SRE: 

1) If you do the rolling 5-minute windows and then count breached windows for monthly credits, how does that map to outage / credit math? Example: if 18 windows breach in a 30-day month (assuming 5m windows), what credit does that equate to under your standard hosted SLA?
2) The outlier exclusion sounds promising. Would Redwood be willing to accept a one-time exception in the hosted SLA to enable the 0.5% exclusion for Acme for the first 6 months while we ramp? We want to avoid frequent fine-grained credits while we optimize request shaping.

We're preparing a short internal note and may include the language you propose in procurement. Amanda

--
Amanda
From: irene.choi@redwood.com
To: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acme.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2026 16:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Measurement window for P50/P95 — need clarification

Amanda — answers below and proposed next steps.

1) Credit math: our hosted SLA defines thresholds in terms of % of breached 5-minute windows per month. Example (illustrative): 
- < 0.1% breached windows: no credit (meets SLA)
- 0.1%–0.5% breached: 5% monthly credit
- 0.5%–1% breached: 15% monthly credit
- >1% breached: 30% monthly credit
We will provide the full table in the redlines document. That mapping is applied to the billed usage for the affected month.

2) Exception request: Redwood is willing to provisionally enable the 0.5% per-window outlier exclusion for Acme for a 6-month trial on the hosted tier as long as: 
- Acme agrees to a monitoring runbook and weekly SRE sync for the first 8 weeks.
- We add a clause that the exclusion can be revoked at 30 days' notice if it materially impacts multi-tenant capacity.

Next steps: Ben will draft the redline language for the SLA appendix and legal will produce the exception clause. Karthik, please add an item to HS-12458 to expose per-tenant monthly percentile in the admin console (estimate: 2 sprints). Amanda — if that works, I'll push the draft exception in the DocuSign packet and share the redlines PDF (attached).

If anyone wants to run the sample calculation with Acme's traffic shapes, Ben and I can pull a synthetic run.

Thanks,
Irene
